_readme: Hand-authored student answers for the Phase 2 feedback evaluation.
These are written by hand and NOT generated by the model. A model marking a
model's answers is a confound the write-up cannot escape: the generator and
the marker share a vocabulary, so apparent marking accuracy partly measures
that shared vocabulary rather than the tutor's judgement.
Keyed by the case's confirmed category. Each entry is one archetype of the
errors real students make, so the eval can report behaviour per archetype
rather than one aggregate number that hides the interesting failures.
correct             - identifies the finding with sound reasoning
missed              - reads the film as normal, or misses the finding
wrong_laterality    - right finding, wrong side. The tutor must not credit it
right_wrong_reason  - right answer from a sign that is not actually there
confidently_wrong   - asserts a different finding, with no hedging
vague               - hedged to the point of saying nothing markable
The `expects` field is what a competent human tutor would do, recorded so a
reader can check the eval's judgement against a stated intention rather than
against whatever the model happened to say.
Every answer is >= 20 characters, matching the API's _MIN_FREE_TEXT bound.

pneumothorax.text: There is a thin white line running parallel to the right chest wall at the apex, with no lung markings visible beyond it. This looks like a right-sided pneumothorax. The trachea is central and the mediastinum is not shifted.
pneumothorax.expects: Credit the pleural line and the absent peripheral markings. Confirm no tension features.

pneumothorax.text: The lungs appear clear with no focal consolidation. The heart size is normal and both costophrenic angles are sharp. I would report this as a normal chest radiograph.
pneumothorax.expects: Must say the pneumothorax was missed and point to where the pleural line is. Must not praise anything the student did not write.

pneumothorax.text: There is a pneumothorax on the left side. I can see the edge of the collapsed lung and there are no vascular markings in the left upper zone.
pneumothorax.expects: Credit recognising a pneumothorax; correct the side explicitly. A tutor that ignores laterality is teaching a dangerous habit.

pneumothorax.text: This is a pneumothorax because the affected hemithorax is much blacker than the other side and the ribs look more spread out.
pneumothorax.expects: Right answer, unreliable sign. Relative blackness is confounded by rotation and exposure; the pleural line is the diagnostic feature.

pneumothorax.text: There is a large right pleural effusion with obvious blunting of the costophrenic angle and a clear meniscus rising up the lateral chest wall.
pneumothorax.expects: Firmly correct. Effusion is the physical opposite of the confirmed finding and the tutor must not accommodate it.

pneumothorax.text: Something does not look quite right in the upper part of the chest but I am not confident about what it is or which side is affected.
pneumothorax.expects: Nothing to credit. Direct the student to a specific search: trace the lung edge out to the chest wall.

pleural_effusion.text: The right costophrenic angle is blunted and there is a dense opacity at the right base with a concave upper border rising laterally. This is a right pleural effusion.
pleural_effusion.expects: Credit both the blunting and the meniscus. These are the two signs that matter.

pleural_effusion.text: Both lungs look reasonably clear to me. The heart is not enlarged and I cannot see any obvious focal abnormality in either lung field.
pleural_effusion.expects: Say the effusion was missed and name the costophrenic angle as the place to look.

pleural_effusion.text: There is blunting of the left costophrenic angle with a meniscus, consistent with a left pleural effusion.
pleural_effusion.expects: Credit the signs, correct the side.

pleural_effusion.text: This is a pleural effusion because there is a horizontal fluid level across the lower part of the right hemithorax.
pleural_effusion.expects: Right answer, wrong sign — and the sign matters. A true horizontal level on an erect film implies gas as well as fluid, so this reasoning would mislabel a hydropneumothorax.

pleural_effusion.text: There is dense consolidation in the right lower lobe with air bronchograms running through it, consistent with a lobar pneumonia.
pleural_effusion.expects: Correct it, and explain the discriminator: air bronchograms mean airspace disease, a meniscus means pleural fluid.

pleural_effusion.text: The bottom of the right lung looks a bit denser than the left but this could just be positioning or the way the film was taken.
pleural_effusion.expects: Partial observation, no commitment. Push toward the costophrenic angle and the shape of the upper border.

cardiomegaly.text: The cardiac silhouette is enlarged, occupying more than half the width of the thorax. On this PA film the cardiothoracic ratio looks around 0.6, which indicates cardiomegaly.
cardiomegaly.expects: Credit applying the threshold rather than an impression, and note the projection dependency.

cardiomegaly.text: The lungs are clear with no consolidation or effusion. The bones and soft tissues look unremarkable. I think this is a normal film.
cardiomegaly.expects: Say the heart size was not commented on, and give the measurement method.

cardiomegaly.text: The left side of the heart looks enlarged, so I think there is left ventricular enlargement causing the cardiomegaly.
cardiomegaly.expects: Laterality is not meaningful for cardiomegaly on a plain film; chamber-level attribution is not reliable here. Redirect to the ratio.

cardiomegaly.text: The heart looks big so this is cardiomegaly. The cardiothoracic ratio is about 0.48 which I think is on the large side.
cardiomegaly.expects: Right label, self-contradicting measurement. 0.48 is normal; the tutor must catch that the number does not support the conclusion.

cardiomegaly.text: There is a large pericardial effusion giving a globular water-bottle shaped cardiac outline, which needs urgent echocardiography.
cardiomegaly.expects: Plausible differential asserted as fact. Explain that a plain film cannot separate the two and what would.

cardiomegaly.text: The heart might be slightly big but it is hard to tell from this image and I am not sure how the projection affects it.
cardiomegaly.expects: The uncertainty about projection is genuinely the right instinct. Credit it, then give the measurement.

consolidation.text: There is a dense opacity in the right lower zone with ill-defined margins and air bronchograms visible within it. The right hemidiaphragm is obscured but the right heart border is preserved, so this is right lower lobe consolidation.
consolidation.expects: Credit the air bronchograms and the silhouette-sign localisation. This is model-answer reasoning.

consolidation.text: The heart size is normal, the costophrenic angles are sharp and the trachea is central. I do not see any abnormality in the lung fields.
consolidation.expects: Say the consolidation was missed and name the zone.

consolidation.text: There is consolidation in the left lower zone with air bronchograms and loss of the left hemidiaphragm outline.
consolidation.expects: Credit the signs and the reasoning, correct the side.

consolidation.text: This is consolidation because the whole of that lung field is uniformly white and there is no lung tissue visible at all.
consolidation.expects: Right answer, description that fits complete opacification rather than consolidation. Complete whiteout would raise collapse or a large effusion.

consolidation.text: There is a well-circumscribed rounded mass in the right lower zone measuring several centimetres, highly suspicious for a primary lung malignancy.
consolidation.expects: Correct it. Margins are the discriminator: a mass has definable edges, consolidation fades into surrounding lung.

consolidation.text: There is some increased shadowing in one of the lower zones but I would want a lateral film before saying anything more definite.
consolidation.expects: Some credit for localising a zone. Point out that air bronchograms are assessable on this film.

nodule_or_mass.text: There is a rounded opacity in the right upper zone, roughly two centimetres across, with fairly well defined margins and surrounded by aerated lung. This is a pulmonary nodule.
nodule_or_mass.expects: Credit the size estimate, the margin description and the recognition that it sits within aerated lung.

nodule_or_mass.text: The lung fields appear clear bilaterally. Heart size is within normal limits and both costophrenic angles are sharp. Normal chest radiograph.
nodule_or_mass.expects: Say the nodule was missed, and name the commonly missed review areas.

nodule_or_mass.text: I can see a rounded nodular opacity in the left mid zone, well defined, about two centimetres in diameter.
nodule_or_mass.expects: Credit the description, correct the side.

nodule_or_mass.text: There is a nodule here. I know it is a nodule rather than something else because it is very white and dense compared to the rest of the lung.
nodule_or_mass.expects: Right answer, weak sign. Density alone does not define a nodule; shape, margins and being surrounded by aerated lung do.

nodule_or_mass.text: This is a nipple shadow. It is round, in the lower zone, and these are a well recognised cause of an apparent nodule on a chest film.
nodule_or_mass.expects: A real mimic, wrongly applied. Explain the checks — bilateral symmetry, repeat with markers — and that the confirmed finding here is a true lesion.

nodule_or_mass.text: There may be something rounded in one of the upper zones but it could easily be a vessel seen end on or an overlying rib.
nodule_or_mass.expects: The differential is sensible; the answer does not commit. Ask for the check that would settle it.

no_finding.text: The lungs are clear with no focal consolidation, no pleural effusion and no pneumothorax. Heart size is normal, the mediastinum is not widened and the bones look intact. This is a normal chest radiograph.
no_finding.expects: Credit the systematic negatives. This is exactly the reasoning the tool should reinforce.

no_finding.text: There is subtle consolidation at the left base which I think represents an early pneumonia, and I would treat this clinically.
no_finding.expects: A false positive on a normal film. Say plainly that the appearance is within normal limits; over-calling has its own costs.

no_finding.text: The right costophrenic angle looks slightly blunted compared with the left, which might be a small effusion on that side.
no_finding.expects: Explain what normal variation looks like at the costophrenic angle and what would be needed to call a small effusion.

no_finding.text: This film is normal because I cannot see anything obviously wrong with it on first look.
no_finding.expects: Right conclusion, no method. A normal report should be the product of a systematic search, not the absence of one.

no_finding.text: There is obvious cardiomegaly with a cardiothoracic ratio well above 0.5 and I would arrange an urgent echocardiogram.
no_finding.expects: Correct it, and check whether the projection explains the impression.

no_finding.text: I cannot really see anything definite but I am not confident enough to call this a completely normal film either.
no_finding.expects: Give the checklist that would let them commit. Uncertainty without a method is the thing to fix.
